prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1445; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at a red light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Claimant reports wrist pain and was transported to the emergency department by ambulance. Claimant has not retained legal counsel at this time.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirmed the left wrist was fractured and is in a splint. Claimant states they are not represented by an attorney and prefers to handle the claim directly. Explained the general claims process and the documentation needed, including medical records and wage verification. Advised claimant to keep all receipts related to treatment and transportation.

Entry 3: Received the emergency department discharge summary. Diagnosis listed as a distal radius fracture, with orthopedic follow-up recommended. Claimant has scheduled a consult with an orthopedic specialist. Photos of both vehicles received from the insured and reviewed. Damage pattern is consistent with the reported impact.

Entry 4: Claimant reports missing time from work due to the injury and has provided an employer letter confirming the absence. Requested pay stubs for the period before the collision. Claimant asked when the property damage portion of the claim will be resolved. Explained that the bodily injury evaluation remains open until treatment is complete and the medical provider releases the claimant to full duty.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Orthopedic consult completed and a cast was applied. Claimant is expected to need further imaging in several weeks. Reminded claimant that a settlement offer cannot be finalized until the treatment course is documented. Claimant was advised again of the right to seek legal advice at any time and agreed to keep the adjuster updated on medical progress. Diary set for follow-up.
